newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain banks off highs after BBV Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Spain banks off highs after BBV Q1 results.

text.p: Spanish banks' shares came off earlier highs on Thursday after Banco Bilbao Vizcaya's (BBV) first quarter earnings met market forecasts, dealers said.
But the breakdown of the data showed that profits on financial operations and provisioning levels outpaced expectations, boding well for BBV's share price, they added.
At 1025 GMT BBV was up 70 pesetas, 0.79 percent, to 8,980 while the Ibex-35 blue chip index added 0.66 percent, to 5,625.20.
BBV, Spain's second-biggest bank, reported 24.73 billion pesetas attributable profit in the three months to March, representing a rise of 24.8 percent.
Provisions rose 10.7 percent to 13.90 billion pesetas while profits on financial operations soared to 19.1 billion from 7.35 billion.

"The surprising thing is that provisions and trading profits are very much higher than expected. The stock is still a buy but with the heights the market has reached at the moment maybe the best thing would be to hold," said a dealer at a Spanish bank.
One trader said the stock had followed the classic pattern of "buy the rumour, sell the news," backing off an all-time high of 9,070 pesetas after this morning's results announcement.
"It's still done very well after climbing around two percent yesterday," he added.
Other banks were also off highs, with most still to report first quarter results.
Banco Central Hispano was up 1.79 percent to 3,985, Santander was up 0.91 percent to 9,990 and Popular added 1.33 percent to 27,420.
Some pinpointed Popular as the best buy among the banks at the moment, having underperformed for some time.
One dealer said in the short term, Popular could go as high as 28,000 pesetas.
